title: [ENT-P02.12] Adopt audited native similarity strategy and parity benchmarks
description:
ENT packet/reference: ENT-P02 child bead under parent bd-3k3. Labels: entity-workbench, child, ent-p02, namekit, similarity, rapidfuzz, licensing.

Purpose/background:
String metrics are useful support evidence, but implementation choice matters for determinism, speed, license, and API fit. RapidFuzz Rust is a strong candidate because it is native Rust, exposes Levenshtein/Jaro-Winkler style metrics, supports byte fast paths, score_cutoff, score_hint, and batch comparators, and is MIT/Apache licensed.

Exact scope:
Evaluate whether to adopt a pinned Rust crate (`rapidfuzz`, `strsim`, or another minimal crate) or implement internal metrics. The decision must include license compatibility, transitive dependency size, determinism, no unsafe policy, ASCII byte path behavior, Unicode char path behavior, cutoff/hint semantics, batch comparator reuse, and benchmark/parity expectations.

Suggested RESERVATIONS:
Cargo.toml; Cargo.lock; src/namekit/similarity.rs; benches/namekit_similarity.rs; tests/namekit/similarity.rs; docs/namekit/similarity-decision.md if a decision note is created.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dependency decision is recorded before code imports a metric crate.
- If adopting RapidFuzz Rust, score_cutoff and score_hint are tested for short-circuit/correctness and cannot change match semantics.
- ASCII byte path is used only when normalization proves ASCII-safe; Unicode path remains correct for non-ASCII fixtures.
- Metric outputs are normalized to stable canon score units with documented rounding.
- Metrics only produce support evidence; they cannot bypass cannot-link or solver constraints.

Verification commands:
cargo test namekit_similarity -- --nocapture; cargo test rapidfuzz_cutoff_hint_parity -- --nocapture; cargo test metric_ascii_unicode_parity -- --nocapture; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings

Tests to add/run later:
RapidFuzz parity examples; empty/long/non-ASCII cases; score_cutoff None/Some cases; score_hint does-not-change-answer tests; basic benchmark for batch comparator reuse.
acceptance_criteria: A dependency decision is recorded before Cargo.toml changes; accepted metrics have parity fixtures for ASCII, Unicode, empty, long, cutoff, score_hint, and batch reuse behavior; metric outputs are normalized into deterministic integer score units; any unsafe/native/transitive-risk concern is escalated before import.

title: [ENT-P02.21] Lock high-recall namekit source-parity implementation decisions
description:
Purpose/background:
The adversarial pass found that namekit is the highest-leverage place to accidentally underbuild the system. A minimal fuzzy matcher would be easier but would produce worse entity-resolution results. This bead locks the quality-oriented implementation decisions before downstream tokenization, sparse indexing, similarity, evidence, and benchmark beads start.

Default decisions:
- Use recall-rich native Rust primitives: word tokens, char n-grams, sparse TF-IDF, rare-token weighting, deterministic top-k, protected-token/cannot-link lanes, and source-parity fixture coverage.
- Dense vectors are forbidden for large corpora. Use integer dictionaries, sorted posting lists, CSR-like offset arrays where useful, and posting-list derived top-k retrieval.
- Sorted-neighborhood is supplemental recall machinery only when deterministic key/window/cap diagnostics are specified; it is not authoritative merge evidence.
- Prefer a pinned native Rust metric crate only after license, unsafe-code, dependency-size, byte/Unicode behavior, cutoff/hint, and parity audits pass. If audit fails, implement required metrics internally rather than weakening parity.
- Scores crossing module/artifact boundaries are deterministic integer score units. No float debug output belongs in artifacts.

title: Robust corpus-scoped OpenFIGI registry provider
description:
Implement a robust canon OpenFIGI registry materialization workflow for known corpora such as CMBS bonds.

Prerequisite note, no official Beads dependency:
Implementation should wait until the twinning REST enhancement can serve the OpenFIGI batch mapping OpenAPI shape. Specifically, twinning must be able to exercise `POST /v3/mapping` with a top-level array request body, per-item success/error responses, OpenFIGI candidate fields, API-key header shape, and 429 retry headers. This epic intentionally records that prerequisite inline rather than adding a Beads dependency edge.

Problem:
OpenFIGI is too large to mirror casually, and querying all possible IDs would create too many API calls. Canon should not become a just-in-time OpenFIGI proxy. For known corpora, canon should materialize only the identifiers present in the corpus into static registry files and use those files offline afterward.

Target architecture:
- The input is a known corpus seed set, for example CMBS CUSIPs/ISINs/SEDOLs extracted from source tapes.
- The seed is normalized, deduped, and split by identifier type before provider calls.
- `canon registry build --source openfigi` queries only unique missing IDs.
- `--incremental` carries forward existing registry entries and fetches only identifiers not already materialized.
- The output remains normal canon registry artifacts: `registry.json`, mapping JSON files, `_build.json`, and local `_index.sqlite` generated by lookup loading.
- Normal `canon` lookup/resolve never calls OpenFIGI. Provider access happens only during controlled registry maintenance.

Implementation tracks:
1. Twinning-backed provider contract tests
- Add a twinned OpenFIGI integration harness once twinning supports the OpenFIGI OpenAPI shape.
- Point canon at the twin through existing `--provider-config base_url=...`.
- Cover success, no match, per-item provider error, ambiguous candidates, malformed/length-mismatched responses, auth header handling, 429 retry handling, and retry header variants.

2. Corpus-scoped materialization workflow
- Document and test the intended workflow for a corpus seed file rather than an all-OpenFIGI crawl.
- Ensure CUSIP/ISIN/SEDOL seeds can be run separately with explicit `id_type` or inferred from `seed_column`.
- Preserve `_build.json` evidence for seed count, queried count, carried-forward count, resolved count, unresolved entries, failures, ambiguity count, API calls, provider options with secrets redacted, and timing.

3. Provider robustness
- Keep response length/order validation strict.
- Treat per-item OpenFIGI `error` as provider failure, empty `data` as unresolved, and multi-candidate ambiguity as an abstention with diagnostics.
- Preserve deterministic candidate selection when one candidate is clearly best; do not introduce fuzzy runtime lookup.
- Keep API-key discovery through `--provider-config api_key=...` or `OPENFIGI_API_KEY` and redact secrets in build artifacts.
- Validate rate limit defaults and explicit `--rate-limit-ms` behavior.

4. Scale guardrails
- Make it clear in docs and tests that query cost is `ceil(unique_missing_ids / batch_size)`, not total corpus rows and not all OpenFIGI IDs.
- Provide practical guidance for CMBS-scale runs: dedupe first, use `--incremental`, set batch/rate limits explicitly for live jobs, and inspect `_build.json` before publishing.
- If tests expose registry file/index scaling problems for large seed sets, add follow-up beads for sharded mapping files, resumable build checkpoints, or bulk SQLite index loading rather than silently widening this epic.

Non-goals:
- Do not mirror all OpenFIGI.
- Do not call OpenFIGI from normal `canon` lookup or `canon resolve`.
- Do not make OpenFIGI the source of truth for organization identity resolution; it may provide securities/instrument evidence, but org canonicalization remains canon/org work.
- Do not require live OpenFIGI credentials for normal tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Twinning prerequisite is satisfied before implementation begins: a twinning REST server can exercise OpenFIGI-compatible `POST /v3/mapping` batch requests and responses. This is documented in the epic body only; no Beads dependency edge is required.
- Canon has twinning-backed tests for the OpenFIGI provider using `--provider-config base_url=...`; normal test runs do not require live OpenFIGI credentials.
- Provider tests cover ordered batch success, partial provider failure, no-match responses, ambiguous candidates, length mismatch refusal, malformed provider payloads, auth header forwarding, 429 retry behavior, `Retry-After`, and `ratelimit-reset`.
- Corpus-scoped workflow is documented for CMBS-style seeds: extract identifiers, normalize/dedupe, split by id type, run separate builds, and publish static registries.
- `registry build --source openfigi --incremental` demonstrably fetches only identifiers missing from the existing registry and reports carried-forward vs queried counts in `_build.json`.
- Generated registry artifacts remain standard static canon registry artifacts and can be used by normal lookup/resolve with no OpenFIGI network access.
- `_build.json` redacts secrets, records provider options, seed hash/count, queried/resolved/unresolved/failure/ambiguous counts, API call count, timing, and generated files.
- Documentation explicitly rejects all-OpenFIGI mirroring and just-in-time OpenFIGI lookup for normal resolution.
- Any large-registry scaling issue discovered during implementation is captured as a follow-up bead rather than hidden behind partial behavior.
- Quality gate passes for code changes: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, and `ubs` on changed files.
notes:
Potential follow-up beads if implementation exposes scale pressure:
- Shard large provider-built mapping files by identifier prefix or hash bucket.
- Add resumable registry build checkpoints for long provider materialization jobs.
- Add bulk SQLite index load optimizations for very large static registries.
- Add a live OpenFIGI smoke test behind explicit environment variables, kept out of normal CI.

Useful command shape after twinning lands:
`canon registry build --source openfigi --seed cmbs-cusips.csv --seed-column cusip --output registries/openfigi-cmbs-cusip --version <version> --incremental --provider-config id_type=ID_CUSIP --provider-config base_url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v3/mapping`

Design boundary:
OpenFIGI belongs in this epic as securities/instrument registry materialization. It should not decide organization identity by itself; organization resolution may consume OpenFIGI-derived evidence later, but canonical org identity remains under canon org resolution rules.

title: [ENT-P09] Audit, promote, sidecars, and exact apply/replay
description:

Purpose:
Close the workbench loop: validate solve outputs against suites and quality gates, promote accepted aliases/sidecars into the exact registry, and replay/apply canonical IDs back onto source rows without mutating raw evidence. Promotion requires exact artifact and registry snapshot continuity.

title: CLI argument parsing (clap derive)
description:
Implement CLI argument parsing using clap derive macros in src/cli.rs.

Struct Cli with:
- input: PathBuf (positional, required unless --version/--describe/--schema)
- registry: PathBuf (--registry, required for processing)
- column: String (--column, required for processing)
- emit: EmitMode enum { Json, Csv } (--emit, default Json)
- canon_column: Option<String> (--canon-column)
- map_out: Option<PathBuf> (--map-out)
- max_rows: Option<usize> (--max-rows)
- max_bytes: Option<u64> (--max-bytes)
- no_witness: bool (--no-witness)
- version: bool (--version, prints 'canon 0.1.0', exit 0)
- describe: bool (--describe, emits operator.json, exit 0)
- schema: bool (--schema, emits canon.v0 JSON Schema, exit 0)

Info commands (--version, --describe, --schema) are self-contained:
- --describe: static operator.json with tool identity (name, version, accepted inputs, output schema, refusal codes)
- --schema: static JSON Schema for the canon.v0 mapping artifact

EmitMode enum: { Json, Csv } with clap ValueEnum derive.
acceptance_criteria: TARGET FILE: src/cli.rs only. Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests. Test: EmitMode parsing, required-arg validation, info command flags. VERIFICATION: cargo test -- cli
notes: operator.json and schema content: author as const &str in cli.rs using include_str! from static JSON files at src/cli/operator.json and src/cli/schema.json (created by this bead, not bd-1do). These are the only additional files this bead creates beyond src/cli.rs. Content: operator.json must include tool name, version, accepted_inputs (csv/jsonl), output_schema ref, refusal_codes (all 10 with descriptions). schema.json must be a valid JSON Schema for the canon.v0 mapping artifact.
close_reason: CLI argument parsing complete - EmitMode enum with Json/Csv variants, full Cli struct with all required fields, info commands with custom version handling, comprehensive tests. Quality gate passes.

title: strategy lifecycle: update, deprecate/remove-from-active-resolution, and promote
description: Add lifecycle operations for registered strategy champions. bd-a43 requires register, update, deprecate-remove, and promote. The implementation must not physically delete entries. Remove means remove from active resolution by marking status deprecated while preserving registry history. RESERVATIONS: src/cli.rs, src/lib.rs, src/strategy_registry.rs.
design: Behavior: update locates one active entry by typed key and skill, replaces script metadata and provenance/proofs as appropriate, requires next-version, keeps key identity stable, and emits before/after receipt state. Deprecate locates one active entry, sets status deprecated, records operator/reason/timestamp, requires next-version, emits receipt state, and makes resolve ignore it without deleting the entry. Promote locates an operator-attested entry, validates verify/assess/airlock using existing proof logic, attaches proof references, changes grade to proof-attested, requires next-version, and emits receipt state. All lifecycle operations refuse ambiguous duplicate active keys; prefer in-place registry mutation over append-only duplicate entries unless the spec deliberately says otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: updating an operator-attested task champion changes script hash and registry version and resolve sees the update; deprecating makes resolve return UNRESOLVED exit 1 without deleting the entry; promoting records proof references and grade proof-attested and lint accepts it; every successful mutation emits before/after registry hashes and source file/entry order in the receipt; invalid lifecycle operations refuse for missing key, not found, deprecated key update without policy, stale next-version, malformed proof, missing operator/reason for deprecate, and ambiguous duplicate active keys; schema-keyed entries follow the documented lifecycle policy.
notes: Prefer command name deprecate over remove; docs can say deprecate is the safe remove-from-active-resolution operation.
close_reason: Implemented strategy v1 typed keys, operator/proof attestation grades, lifecycle, catalog/explain, receipts/witness, lint/diff/docs/tests; verified cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, cargo build --release --locked, and UBS on changed files.

title: canon strategy: intent-keyed champions + operator-attested grade
description:
Umbrella feature for making canon strategy fit real operator workflows where the reusable artifact is an intent-triggered script, not a script tied to a columnar input profile.

Current state:
- canon strategy is implemented as a versioned local registry under _strategy/*.json.
- Existing entries are keyed by (schema_fingerprint, skill_hash).
- Existing register requires verify, assess, and airlock proof artifacts.
- Existing resolve can return EXACT, COMPATIBLE, PARTIAL, or UNRESOLVED by comparing schema shapes.

Target state:
- The same strategy registry supports typed keys: schema-shape keys and task/intent keys.
- Task/intent keys are scoped by skill hash: (key_type=task, task=<declared intent>, skill_hash=<BLAKE3 skill hash>).
- Task-keyed resolve is exact: EXACT when an active champion exists, UNRESOLVED otherwise. Schema tiers are not applicable for task keys.
- Entries carry an attestation grade: operator-attested or proof-attested.
- Operator-attested registration is the lightweight v1 path for a new user: save a script that just worked, without requiring verify/assess/airlock or any external tooling.
- Proof-attested registration remains the heavier path using audit/proof artifacts.
- Lifecycle operations support register, update, deprecate/remove-from-active-resolution, and promote operator-attested entries to proof-attested entries by attaching proof artifacts later.

Non-goals for this graph:
- No tournament or NTM multi-agent implementation.
- No script execution during strategy resolve.
- No deletion of registry entries. Remove means mark deprecated/inactive so git history and registry auditability remain intact.
design:
Use the existing strategy registry instead of building a side registry. The correct implementation path is to generalize the current entry schema and registry operations while preserving existing proof-attested, schema-keyed behavior as a first-class mode.

The graph is intentionally ordered so contract/spec work comes first, then the data model and CLI validation, then behavior paths, then lint/diff/docs/tests/quality. This keeps later beads self-contained and prevents implementers from guessing about JSON shape or CLI semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
The feature is complete only when a human can run and inspect a standalone flow on a fresh machine:
1. Register a task-keyed script with operator identity, timestamp, and one-line reason, with no fixture suite and no verify/assess/airlock inputs.
2. Resolve the same task and skill to the frozen script with EXACT exit 0, and UNRESOLVED exit 1 when no active task entry exists.
3. List and explain registered strategy champions, including typed key, grade, status, provenance, source file, entry order, and why resolve would choose or ignore an entry.
4. Update the champion with a version bump and a deterministic mutation receipt.
5. Deprecate/remove the champion from active resolution without deleting registry history.
6. Promote an operator-attested champion to proof-attested by attaching audit/proof artifacts later.
7. Emit deterministic receipts and witness records for mutating strategy commands without recording raw script bytes or secrets.
8. Run existing proof-attested schema-keyed strategy workflows unchanged as intentional product behavior.
9. Prove the mixed registry contract through reusable matrix coverage for schema proof, task operator, task promoted proof, and deprecated task entries.
10. Pass registry lint, strategy diff, README/operator docs checks, CLI smoke tests, br graph validation, and the full Rust quality gate.

title: canon registry add-entry: atomic single-alias-entry write + semver bump + lint
description:
Add `canon registry add-entry` as the safe single-alias writer for self-authored registries.

Purpose:
- Replace hand-editing mapping JSON with a deterministic write path that validates one new alias, bumps registry metadata, and leaves the registry in a state the normal exact lookup path can consume.
- This is registry maintenance, not a resolution workbench: no matching, no suggestions, no fuzzy behavior.

CLI:
`canon registry add-entry --registry <DIR> --alias-file <FILE> --canonical-id <ID> --input <INPUT> --rule-id <RULE> [--canonical-type <TYPE>] [--bump patch|minor|major | --next-version <VER>] [--no-lint] [--emit json|plain]`

Behavior:
- `--alias-file` must be an existing root-level mapping file name ending in `.json`; reject paths, subdirectories, `registry.json`, and `_build.json`.
- Parse all root mapping files using the existing flat registry rules before planning the write.
- Refuse if `--input` is empty after ASCII trim or is not already in trimmed form. The value written should be exactly what future lookup receives after input trim.
- Refuse if any existing mapping entry anywhere in the registry already has the same `input`, regardless of `rule_id`. First-match-wins lookup makes duplicate inputs unsafe for this writer.
- `--canonical-type` is required for a new canonical ID. If omitted for an existing canonical ID, infer it only when all existing entries for that canonical ID use exactly one canonical_type; otherwise refuse.
- If `registry.json.default_id_scheme` exists, validate `--canonical-id` against that scheme unless the command is later extended with an explicit override flag. Do not silently write out-of-scheme IDs for self-authored registries.
- Version update: accept either `--next-version <VER>` or `--bump patch|minor|major`, but not both. Default is `--bump patch`. If the current version cannot be parsed as numeric `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, refuse and require `--next-version`.
- Increment `entry_count` by one and preserve all other `registry.json` fields, including unknown metadata.
- Validate proposed output before commit. If `--no-lint` is not set, run the standard lint check and abort on lint errors; warnings/info are reported in the JSON receipt but do not block.
- Write mapping file and `registry.json` using temp-file-then-rename or an equivalent restore-on-failure sequence. A failed validation, lint error, or write error must leave the original files byte-for-byte intact.
- Do not directly mutate `_index.sqlite`; the version change should cause normal registry loading to rebuild the derived index.
- Do not add new witness behavior in this bead. Keep registry command side effects limited to the documented registry file writes.

Output:
- Default `--emit json`: emit `canon_registry_add_entry.v0` with registry before/after, alias entry, touched files, lint summary, and warnings.

title: External prerequisite: twinning REST supports OpenFIGI batch mapping OpenAPI
description:
This is a canon-side blocker representing work owned by twinning. Do not implement canon OpenFIGI robustness work against a mock-only contract until the twinning REST enhancement can execute the OpenFIGI mapping API shape.

Required twinning capability:
- Serve an OpenAPI-described `POST /v3/mapping` endpoint compatible with OpenFIGI mapping semantics.
- Accept a top-level JSON array request body of mapping jobs with at least `idType` and `idValue`.
- Return a top-level JSON array response in the same order and length as the request.
- Support per-item success via `{ "data": [...] }` and per-item failure via `{ "error": "..." }`.
- Support candidate fields used by canon: `figi`, `compositeFIGI`, `ticker`, `name`, `securityType`, and `exchCode`.
- Enforce or observe `X-OPENFIGI-APIKEY` auth shape.
- Exercise 429 responses with `Retry-After` or `ratelimit-reset` headers so canon retry behavior can be tested.
- Provide deterministic seeded/replayed cases for success, miss, provider error, ambiguity, malformed/length-mismatched response, and rate-limit retry.

Close this blocker only when a canon test or documented smoke command can point `canon registry build --source openfigi` at a twinning `base_url` and receive OpenFIGI-shaped responses without using live OpenFIGI.
close_reason: Superseded by inline prerequisite note in the canon OpenFIGI epic per user direction; no dependency gate needed.

title: Resolve v0 scoring and match decisions
description:
Implement deterministic candidate scoring and match decision logic for canon resolve.

Scope:
- Add src/resolve/scoring.rs.
- For each target record, score each surviving reference candidate by evaluating strategy assertions in YAML order.
- Apply assertion weights and required-assertion semantics.
- Compute total candidate score and assertion evidence details.
- Select the best candidate using deterministic ordering, including lexicographic reference ID tie-breaking when scores are equal.
- Apply match_threshold and ambiguity_gap.
- Classify each target as MATCHED, UNMATCHED, or AMBIGUOUS.
- Include runner-up data for matches and near-miss data for unmatched records.
- Detect and report v0 one-to-many conflicts where multiple target records choose the same reference record, without trying to solve global bipartite matching yet.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover high-confidence match, below-threshold unmatched, insufficient ambiguity gap, exact score ties, required assertion failure, runner-up gap calculation, near-miss reporting, and same-reference conflict warnings.
- Output ordering is stable across repeated runs.
- Floating-point comparisons are deterministic and avoid platform-sensitive ordering surprises where practical.
- No registry write-back occurs here; this bead only produces in-memory decision records.

Target files:
- src/resolve/scoring.rs
- src/resolve/types.rs if needed
- tests/fixtures/resolve/** only if fixture adjustments are needed

Reservation guidance:
- Reserve only scoring-related files and exact fixture files touched.

- V0 can be simple, but the graph boundary should be explicit so v1 can add bipartite constraints and neighborhood signals later.

- Build a petgraph graph from loaded reference and target records.
- Insert nodes in sorted composite-ID order for deterministic traversal.
- Apply strategy candidate_filter entries in declaration order.
- Candidate filters should narrow reference candidates per target using operators such as exact, canon_match, range, date_range, prefix, and any explicitly supported subset from the strategy parser.
- Enforce max_candidates from strategy/CLI and refuse with E_TOO_MANY_CANDIDATES when a target has too many surviving candidates.
- Emit structured candidate provenance so output/scoring can explain which filters passed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests cover node counts, side labels, deterministic node ordering, candidate filtering by exact/range/canon_match, max-candidate refusal, and no-candidate behavior.
- Candidate filtering avoids full output cross-product in normal fixture cases but remains deterministic when filters are absent.
- The graph is ephemeral and no graph state is written to the registry or disk.

- src/resolve/types.rs if needed

title: strategy register: operator-attested task champions without proof tooling
description: Implement the lightweight v1 register path: save a script that just worked as an operator-attested strategy champion. The target user flow should stand alone on a new user's machine and require no verify, assess, airlock, fixture suite, NTM, or multi-agent tooling. RESERVATIONS: src/strategy_registry.rs, src/lib.rs.
design:
Behavior: register task-keyed operator-attested entries into the same _strategy/entries.json used by existing champions; require explicit next-version different from registry.json version; require task, skill identity, script path, script-id, language, operator identity, and one-line reason; hash skill and script bytes with BLAKE3; record operator attestation provenance including operator, attested_at, reason, script content hash, and attestation hash; allow explicit attested_at if the spec adopts it for deterministic tests, defaulting to current UTC only for live CLI; refuse duplicate active key registration and point users to update or deprecate.

Successful register emits a receipt with registry id, before/after version, before/after registry hash, typed key, grade/status, script metadata, source file/entry order, and next suggested commands. It must provide the data needed by the witness parity bead without forcing resolve/list/explain to mutate state.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: task-keyed operator-attested register succeeds without --verify, --assess, or --airlock; registry.json version and entry_count update exactly once; _strategy/entries.json remains pretty-printed deterministic JSON with entry_schema_version; registered entry immediately resolves by task and skill with EXACT; duplicate active register refuses with next_command; success JSON includes a deterministic mutation receipt; existing proof-attested schema register remains supported and proof-gated.

title: [ENT-P13.6] Freeze sec10d parser-evidence immutability and Snowflake append-only contract
description:
Purpose/background:
sec10d is parser-first. canon entity may consume org_mentions-shaped observations and append canonical enrichment, but it must not rewrite parser evidence or silently change Snowflake-facing contracts.

Exact scope:
Freeze the sec10d org_mentions input contract and append-only enriched output contract. Cover source_row_id, record_id, dataset, field_name, org_name, doc_id, filing CIK/accession/form/period fields, role/capacity/platform/subject-role fields, deal_key, transaction_name, alias_surfaces_json, and mention_surfaces_json. Define byte-preservation checks for raw fields and deterministic appended canonical fields.

Concrete assertions:
- org_mentions.csv/JSONL fixture is accepted directly by regab_firm_identity prepare without sec10d parser rewrites.

- PNC vs Midland, bank vs loan-services division, platform/category labels, auditor/subject-role conflicts, and parent/subsidiary cases are distinct/review/escrow unless reviewed policy says otherwise.

title: [ENT-P13.7] Freeze local sec10d contract fixture snapshots inside canon
description:
Purpose/background:
The adversarial pass found that sec10d compatibility cannot depend on a moving external repo shape. canon entity needs local fixture snapshots that define the Reg AB org_mentions input contract, parser-field preservation, Snowflake append-only output, and hard-negative review behavior.

Exact scope:
Create canon-owned sec10d contract fixtures for org_mentions CSV/JSONL input and enriched output. The fixture set should be small but semantically complete: PNC vs Midland, platform/category label, auditor vs subject-party role conflict, parent/subsidiary or bank/division distinction, alias_surfaces_json, mention_surfaces_json, raw parser provenance fields, and expected appended canonical fields.

Required fixture properties:
- accepted directly by regab_firm_identity prepare without sec10d parser rewrites.
- raw parser fields are byte-preserved through apply/enrich where the format permits.
- enrichment appends only the approved *_org_* canonical fields plus explicit unresolved/reviewable status.
- hard-negative examples remain distinct/review/escrow unless an explicit reviewed policy fixture says otherwise.

title: [ENT-P13.8] Add sec10d Reg AB baseline benchmark suite
description:
Purpose/background:
Use the supplied public sec10d Reg AB baseline zip at /Users/zacharyruiz/Downloads/sec10d_regab_org_canon_baseline_20260623T204557Z.zip to prove use case #2 with real downstream data, not test theatre. The baseline has 127,991 firm mentions, 46 unique raw firm surfaces, 31 canonical ids, 0 unresolved mentions, registry firms version 1.0.12, and append-only enriched JSONL outputs.

Exact scope:
Implement the benchmark contract documented in docs/SEC10D_REGAB_BENCHMARKS.md and tests/fixtures/entity/regab/sec10d_regab_benchmark_manifest.json. Normal CI must use the committed compact public-data slice under tests/fixtures/entity/regab/sec10d_baseline_public, which includes one real row per observed firm surface, matching canonized rows, expected lookup output, small enriched JSONL samples, and the firms registry snapshot. Operator-tier checks may additionally run against the full baseline zip.

Required behavior:
- Do not commit the full 660MB-class raw baseline zip; commit only benchmark-relevant public fixture slices and discard the rest.
- REGAB-SRC-001 and REGAB-OBS-001 assert fixed source hashes, row counts, columns, and dataset/field counts for the full baseline tier.
- REGAB-OBS-002 asserts the committed public fixture slice covers all 46 observed surfaces and all 31 canonical ids.
- REGAB-LOOKUP-001 asserts all 46 baseline surfaces map to the manifest canonical id and rule id.
- REGAB-APPLY-001 and REGAB-ENRICH-001 prove sec10d parser evidence remains append-only and Snowflake-facing fields are stable.
- REGAB-HIER-001/002 prevent PNC/Midland and Wells Fargo bank/servicing division over-merges.
- REGAB-ALIAS-001 requires explicit reviewed rule lanes for punctuation, case, compliance-statement prefixes, predecessor aliases, and subsidiaries wording.
- REGAB-PREP-001 and REGAB-PERF-001 prove unique-surface/dedupe-first behavior, not row-level all-pairs work.

Suggested RESERVATIONS:
docs/SEC10D_REGAB_BENCHMARKS.md; tests/fixtures/entity/regab/sec10d_regab_benchmark_manifest.json; tests/fixtures/entity/regab/sec10d_baseline_public/*; tests/entity/sec10d_regab_baseline_benchmark.rs; tests/perf/entity_sec10d_regab_baseline.rs if performance tier helpers are added.

Acceptance criteria:
A future implementation agent can run or implement every REGAB-* benchmark from the doc/manifest and committed public fixture slice; every benchmark has a behavioral assertion; no benchmark passes solely because an artifact exists; failures explain whether source compatibility, exact replay, parser preservation, alias policy, hierarchy anti-collapse, review handling, determinism, or performance structure regressed.

title: CLI e2e smoke: fixtureless task champion flow with detailed diagnostics
description: Add end-to-end CLI coverage for the primary bd-a43 user story. A human should be able to save a script that just worked, resolve it by task, update it, deprecate it, and promote it later. This must be proven through the compiled canon binary, not only internal unit tests. RESERVATIONS: tests/cli_smoke.rs.
design: Test scenario: create temp strategy registry with registry.json; create SKILL.md and sql_lineage.py in tempdir; register task sql_lineage as operator-attested with operator and reason and no proof artifacts; assert mutation receipt and witness behavior; resolve task and assert EXACT, script id/path/hash, grade, registry version, and exit 0; list and explain the champion and assert they agree with resolve; update script and assert receipt plus resolve sees new script hash/id as specified; deprecate task and assert resolve returns UNRESOLVED exit 1 while explain shows deprecated history; re-register or use fresh registry as needed, then promote with proof artifacts and assert grade proof-attested.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: test fails with useful stdout/stderr context when any command refuses unexpectedly; asserts no verify/assess/airlock artifacts are needed for operator-attested register; asserts proof artifacts are needed for promote/proof-attested behavior; asserts receipts include before/after hashes and no raw script bytes; asserts witness append and suppression behavior in temp paths; asserts list/explain are deterministic and match resolve; existing strategy CLI smoke tests for schema-keyed proof-attested register/resolve continue to pass; test uses tempdir-generated files and no external services or NTM tooling.
